chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Yahya al-Taweel, Sahib al-Minqari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is sufficient for the believer's honor that when he sees an evil, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows of his denial of it in his heart.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for a believer to be considered honorable when facing evil?
ai.summary: In the context of Shia jurisprudence on the 'Four Degrees of Commanding Good and Forbidding Evil,' this hadith from al-Kafi establishes the lowest yet essential level: denial by the heart (inkar al-qalb). It signifies that even when physical or verbal action is impossible due to fear or weakness, sincere internal rejection of sin preserves the believer's spiritual dignity and is fully known to Allah. This concept underscores the principle that faith is rooted in the heart, serving as the foundation for higher degrees of outward action.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Yahya Al taweel Sahib Al Minqary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The believer would be Reckoned with honourably when he sees an evil, if Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Knows of his denial of it in his heart’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Yahya al-‘ Attar Sahib al-Minqariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

It is enough in terms of honor for a believing person who upon seeing an evil act committed informs (if he finds) Allah, the most Majestic, the most Glorious, that he rejects and denounces such act.’”
